top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) is a single, well-defined invention, the magic-wavelength condition, that was predicted, realised and then independently reproduced at the 1e-18 level in Sr, Yb and Hg on several continents, and has been used to look at nature (millimetre gravitational redshift, bounds on varying constants and dark-matter couplings). The credit is the cleanest on the table, and the citation can be tied to the lattice concept to separate it from the 2005 and 2012 timekeeping prizes. P002 (hexatic melting) is a testable and experimentally checked prediction but overlaps with the 2016 prize and has one supporter; I still rank it above no award because the physics is real and the laureate trio is unambiguous.
